topic_name: Power Play: Can Folded Paper Reach the Moon?
title: Each fold doubles the stack
description: Shows a folded sheet doubling its layers with every fold and asks whether 46 folds could reach the Moon.

title: Each fold doubles the thickness
description: Shows a sheet 0.001 cm thick becoming 0.002, 0.004 and 0.008 cm as it is folded once, twice and three times.

title: Fold 26 and fold 30 against real heights
description: Compares the stack after 26 folds (about 670 m) with the 830 m Burj Khalifa, and after 30 folds (about 10.7 km) with the 11 km depth of the Mariana Trench.

title: Every 10 folds multiply by 1024
description: Shows that the thickness at fold 0, fold 10 and fold 20 grows by the same factor 1024 each time.

title: The 46th fold passes the Moon
description: Shows that fold 45 (about 351844 km) is still short of the Moon at 384400 km, and doubling once more to fold 46 (about 703687 km) passes it.

topic_name: Exponential Notation: Powers, Bases and Exponents
title: Base and exponent in 5⁴
description: Names the base 5 and the exponent 4 in 5⁴ and shows it means four 5s multiplied, which is 625.

topic_name: Exponential Notation: Powers, Bases and Exponents
title: Adding 4s against multiplying 4s
description: Contrasts 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 with 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 so that repeated multiplication is seen to grow much faster.

topic_name: Exponential Notation: Powers, Bases and Exponents
title: Even or odd number of negative factors
description: Compares (−2)⁴ = 16, where all negative factors pair up, with (−4)³ = −64, where one factor is left without a partner.

topic_name: Exponential Notation: Powers, Bases and Exponents
title: 32400 as powers of primes
description: Shows the ten prime factors of 32400 sorted into three groups, written as 2⁴ × 5² × 3⁴.

topic_name: Exponential Notation: Powers, Bases and Exponents
title: A strip of factors becomes a power
description: Shows the core move of the practice tool: a strip of four 6s is written as 6⁴ and multiplied out to 1296.

topic_name: Multiplying Powers of the Same Base
title: Rooms times diamonds in a room
description: Shows seven factors of 3 split into 3⁴ = 81 rooms and 3³ = 27 diamonds per room, giving 81 × 27 = 2187 diamonds.

topic_name: Multiplying Powers of the Same Base
title: Joining strips adds the exponents
description: Shows p⁴ and p to the power 6 joined into one strip of 10 p's, so the exponents add.

topic_name: Multiplying Powers of the Same Base
title: Two groups of three 4s
description: Shows (4³)² as two groups of three 4s, six 4s in all, so (4³)² = 4⁶ = 4096.

topic_name: Multiplying Powers of the Same Base
title: Six 8s grouped two ways
description: Shows the same six factors of 8 grouped as three pairs, (8²)³, and as two triples, (8³)².

topic_name: Multiplying Powers of the Same Base
title: Join two strips: the exponents add
description: Shows the product rule as joining a strip of three factors of 2 and a strip of two factors of 2 into one strip of five, 2³ × 2² = 2⁵.

title: Half covered the day before full
description: Compares the pond on day 29, half covered, with day 30, fully covered, because the lotuses double each day.

title: Pair each 2 with a 3
description: Shows 2⁴ × 3⁴ as four pairs of a 2 and a 3, each pair making 6, so 2⁴ × 3⁴ = 6⁴ = 1296.

title: Pair each 10 with a 5
description: Shows 10⁴ ÷ 5⁴ as four 10s over four 5s, each column giving 2, so the result is 2⁴, which is 16.

title: Three ways to write one number
description: Shows that 2⁴ × 3⁶, 6⁴ × 3² and 18² × 6² all rewrite to 2⁴ × 3⁶, which is 11664.

title: 3 caps times 4 dresses
description: Shows a tree of choices: each of Estu's 3 caps goes with each of 4 dresses, making 12 outfits.

title: Five slots, ten choices each
description: Shows a 5-digit lock as five slots with 10 choices each, giving 10⁵ = 100000 passwords.

title: Six slots of 26 letters
description: Shows a lock with 6 letter slots, each with 26 choices, giving 26 to the power 6 passwords.

title: Five slots, thirty six choices each
description: Shows an alphanumeric code of length 5 as five slots with 36 choices each, giving 36⁵ = 60466176 codes.

topic_name: Dividing Powers of the Same Base
title: Halving 16 again and again
description: Shows a line of 16 units halved to 8, 4 and 2, with each length written as a power of 2.

topic_name: Dividing Powers of the Same Base
title: Cancel 25 twos from 100 twos
description: Shows 2¹⁰⁰ ÷ 2²⁵ as a long strip of 100 factors over a short strip of 25, where the 25 cancel and 75 are left, so the quotient is 2⁷⁵.

topic_name: Dividing Powers of the Same Base
title: Cancel pairs across the bar
description: Shows the core move of the practice tool: in 3⁵ ÷ 3², two matching pairs cancel and three 3s are left.

title: Everything cancels, so 2⁰ = 1
description: Shows 2⁴ ÷ 2⁴ with all four factors cancelling, leaving 1, and the rule giving 2⁰, so 2⁰ = 1.

title: Halving past one unit
description: Shows the halving of 16 continued past 1 unit to half a unit, which is written as 2 with exponent −1.

title: Each step down divides by 10
description: Shows 1 divided by 10 three times reaching 1/1000, which is 10 to the power −3, a small positive number and not a negative one.

title: A negative exponent moves below the bar
description: Shows 2 with exponent −4 rewritten as 1 over 2⁴, which is 1/16.

title: Add the exponents, even negative ones
description: Shows 2 to the power −4 × 2⁷ on a line of exponents: a jump of −4 then a jump of +7 lands on 3, so the product is 2³.

title: Stepping down the powers of 2
description: Shows the core move of the practice tool: each step down the staircase of powers of 2 divides by 2, giving 2⁰ = 1 and 2 with exponent −1 equal to 1/2.

title: Three steps down the power line of 4
description: Shows the powers of 4 from 4³ to 4⁸ on a line, with 65536 ÷ 64 as a move of 3 steps down from 4⁸ to 4⁵.

title: 16384 is 16 times 1024
description: Shows that 4 to the power 7 is 16 copies of 4 to the power 5, because their quotient is 4², which is 16.

title: Four steps up the power line of 7
description: Shows 343 × 2401 on the power line of 7 as a move of 4 steps up from 7³ to 7⁷, which is 823543.

title: Place values are powers of 10
description: Shows 5642 in a place value chart whose column headings are 10³, 10², 10¹ and 10⁰.

title: Move the point until one digit is left
description: Shows 5900 written as 5.9 × 10³ by moving the decimal point 3 places to the left.

title: Change the exponent, not the coefficient
description: Compares 2 × 10⁷ with 3 × 10⁷ and with 2 × 10 to the power 8 using bars drawn to scale.

title: Where the Earth sits between the Sun and Saturn
description: Shows the Sun to Saturn distance, 1.4335 × 10¹² m, on a line, with the Earth at 1.496 × 10¹¹ m, about one tenth of the way.

title: Count the places the point moves
description: Shows 3430000 written as 3.43 × 10⁶ by moving the decimal point 6 places to the left.

title: Bigger base, smaller power
description: Shows the cards 4³ and 3⁴ with bars of 64 and 81 from one baseline, so 3⁴ is larger.

topic_name: Did You Ever Wonder? Guess, Model, Estimate
title: Worth of an offering on a balance
description: Shows Roxie balanced by an equal weight of jaggery, so the worth is 45 × 70 = 3150 rupees.

topic_name: Did You Ever Wonder? Guess, Model, Estimate
title: Coins that balance a weight
description: Shows a balance with a 45 kg weight against a heap of 1-rupee coins of about 4 g each, about 11250 coins.

topic_name: Did You Ever Wonder? Guess, Model, Estimate
title: Walking around the Earth
description: Shows the estimate: 70 years of non-stop walking at 5 km an hour covers 3066000 km, about 76 times around the 40000 km Earth.

topic_name: Did You Ever Wonder? Guess, Model, Estimate
title: Adding steps against doubling folds
description: Compares a ladder of 20 cm steps that needs 1922000000 steps to reach the Moon with paper folds that need only 46 doublings.

topic_name: Did You Ever Wonder? Guess, Model, Estimate
title: 5 more bottles every day
description: Shows the container problem as linear growth: 5 bottles added each day, giving 200 after 40 days.

topic_name: Getting a Sense for Large Numbers
title: Populations on a powers of 10 line
description: Places elephants, starlings, people and mosquitoes on one line marked in powers of 10.

topic_name: Getting a Sense for Large Numbers
title: Divide coefficients, subtract exponents
description: Shows ants per human: 2 × 10 to the power 16 divided by 8 × 10 to the power 9 gives 2.5 × 10 to the power 6.

topic_name: Getting a Sense for Large Numbers
title: One age, three units
description: Shows Roxie's age of 4840 days becoming 116160 hours and 6969600 minutes.

topic_name: Getting a Sense for Large Numbers
title: A time scale in powers of 10
description: Places a ball falling, a cup of tea, about 11.57 days and about 31 years on a scale where each step is 10 times the last.

topic_name: Getting a Sense for Large Numbers
title: Multiply coefficients, add exponents
description: Shows 10⁸ colonies times 5 × 10⁴ bees each giving 5 × 10¹² bees.

topic_name: A Pinch of History: Names for Powers of 10
title: Each Indian name is a hundred times more
description: Shows lakh, crore, arab and kharab as steps of 10⁵, 10⁷, 10⁹ and 10 to the power 11, each a hundred times the one before.

topic_name: A Pinch of History: Names for Powers of 10
title: Each name is a thousand times the last
description: Shows thousand, million, billion and trillion as a staircase where each step multiplies by 1000, and a googol, 10¹⁰⁰, far above.

topic_name: A Pinch of History: Names for Powers of 10
title: What bi and tri count
description: Shows a billion as 1000 with 2 more 1000s multiplied on, and a trillion as 1000 with 3 more, so the first part of the name counts them.

title: Powers in three cards
description: Sums up the chapter in three cards: what a power means, one exponent rule, and standard form.
